candidate.answerReason: The cosine difference formula gives \(\cos(180^\circ-\alpha)=-\cos\alpha\) for every real angle \(\alpha\).

methods.label: Use the cosine difference identity
methods.explanation: The cosine difference identity gives \[\cos(180^\circ-\alpha)=\cos180^\circ\cos\alpha+\sin180^\circ\sin\alpha=-\cos\alpha.\] This holds for every real angle \(\alpha\), so C is correct.
methods.levelReason: Uses high-school angle sum/difference formula knowledge and trigonometric values on the axes.

methods.label: Reflect the unit-circle point
methods.explanation:
For any real angle \(\alpha\), its unit-circle point is \((\cos\alpha,\sin\alpha)\). Reflection across the \(y\)-axis changes its direction angle to \(180^\circ-\alpha\), up to a whole number of turns, and changes its coordinates to \((-\cos\alpha,\sin\alpha)\). Cosine is the horizontal coordinate, so
\[\cos(180^\circ-\alpha)=-\cos\alpha.\]
Thus C is correct for every real \(\alpha\).
methods.levelReason: Uses unit-circle definitions, coordinate reflection and coterminal angles, without requiring an angle-difference formula.
